turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's clarify the concept of even numbers. In mathematics, an even number is any integer that can be divided evenly by 2. So when we have 2n, it means we have a number that is divisible by 2. Can you think of any examples of even numbers that fit this definition?

turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that even numbers can be divided by 2, like 4 or 6. But I still don't really understand why 2n is always even. If n is any number, can't it just be anything? Like, what if n was 1? Wouldn't that just make it 2, which is even, but what about other numbers?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's focus on the specific case of 2n. Remember that in this context, n represents any integer. So when we substitute different values for n, we always end up with a number that is divisible by 2. Can you try substituting a few different values for n and see if you notice a pattern with the results?
